newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU to continue to work for Cyprus solution.
newsitem.headline: EU to continue to work for Cyprus solution.

text.p: The European Commission, saying it would regret any obstacles in the search for a political solution in Cyprus, vowed on Monday to keep urging both sides on the divided island to talk to settle their differences.
"We continue to encourage both parties to seek a negotiated solution to their differences," said Commission spokesman Joao Vale de Almeida.

He was commenting on last week's failed U.N. talks in Switzerland aimed at breaking decades of division in Cyprus. The five-day session ended in disarray on Friday with Greek and Turkish Cypriot leaders wrangling in public.

The spokesman was specifically asked to react to a threat by Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash to pull out of U.N. negotiations if talks between Cyprus and the EU go ahead early next year. The EU decided two years ago to open entry talks with Cyprus in 1998.

But Greek Cypriot leader Glafcos Clerides, president of the internationally recognised Cypriot government which will negotiate on behalf of Cyprus, has vowed to pull out of any settlement negotiations if EU plans are delayed.
Vale de Almeida reiterated that there had to be politically negotiated solution on the island. "We have a strong position on this and we have not changed our view."
Cypriot Greeks and Turks have been estranged since 1963 when a government in which both took part collapsed amid violence.
Turkey invaded the northern third in 1974 after a coup in the capital Nicosia engineered by the rightist junta then ruling Greece.

U.N. mediator and special Cyprus envoy Diego Cordovez, talking to reporters on Friday after five days of fruitless talks, said he had accepted an invitation from both sides to visit the Mediterranean island at a future date.
Talks would continue on humanitarian issues, he said. But he had no date for a new round.
